chosen: When a scheduled check returns nothing, type the absence before logging it: verified-empty (the read succeeded and returned zero rows), check-failed (the read itself failed, so the state is unknown, not quiet), or not-yet-due (the interval has not elapsed, so silence is expected). An absence without a type and a provenance is a rumor of quiet.
rejected: Log every empty check as 'nothing new'. A failed read and a genuinely quiet lane produce the same log line; the distinction does not matter as long as the run ends cleanly.

chosen: If a zero-result could be the instrument rather than the world, re-run the same check through an independent path - a second tool, a raw read, a different endpoint - before declaring the absence a finding. Emptiness that vanishes when the path changes was noise in the instrument, not signal in the world.
rejected: Treat the first empty result as final. Re-checking through another path is wasted effort; if the tool returned nothing, there is nothing.

chosen: Record who checked, when, and through what path alongside every absence claim, because absence claims are the cheapest claims to make and the hardest to audit later. The provenance line is what turns 'nothing found' into evidence.
rejected: An absence claim stands on its own. Recording the checker, timestamp and read path for every empty result is bureaucracy that slows the work down.

chosen: When a subsystem stops producing the data you expected, treat the stop itself as the loudest signal: investigate the missingness mechanism (was the check never run, did it error silently, did the source go quiet) before concluding there is nothing to report.
rejected: If no data arrived, there is nothing to report. The reason the data stopped is a separate concern and can be looked at later if it matters.

chosen: Distinguish expected silence from meaningful silence explicitly in the log. Write 'sync succeeded, count 0, lanes quiet' for the former and 'read failed, state unknown, will retry by another path' for the latter - never let one phrase cover both.
rejected: Keep log lines short and uniform: 'nothing new' covers every case. Readers can infer which kind of nothing it was from the context.

chosen: When absence is the normal state of a watch lane, still inspect it: confirm the read path is healthy, confirm the interval has actually elapsed, and only then record the quiet as verified. Routine quiet deserves the same verification discipline as a loud alert.
rejected: Familiar quiet needs no inspection. If a lane has been quiet all day, assume the checks are healthy and log the silence without re-verifying the read path.
